# Getting AI Assistants to Recommend Your Company

Getting recommended by ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, and Google AI Overviews falls under a discipline often called **GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)** or **AEO (Answer Engine Optimization)**. Here's a practical playbook based on current best practices:

## 1. Start With a Baseline Audit

Before changing anything, find out where you currently stand. Check where you currently appear across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Mode for your category's most valuable queries, and set your baseline so you can measure improvement.

To do this:
- Pull 20 to 30 real questions from your sales calls, support tickets, and reviews, using your buyers' exact language, not your marketing team's interpretation of it.
- Build your list around the questions customers use when choosing between products or services — category and "best" queries, specific use cases, problems they need to solve, comparisons, alternatives, budgets, and location-specific searches. Start with 20–50 questions that have clear commercial value.
- Note that running the same question more than once, or phrased slightly differently, will often produce different answers, so track the pattern across a few runs rather than treating any single answer as the verdict.

## 2. Fix the Technical Foundation

- Google says AI features rely on the same core SEO principles as Search, with no additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode. OpenAI similarly recommends allowing OAI-SearchBot to crawl your site if you want to be surfaced in ChatGPT's search results.
- Make sure your pages are indexed and crawlable — confirm the post is indexed, the SEO title and meta description are visible, the focus keyphrase is present naturally, all internal links work, and the FAQ schema validates.

## 3. Structure Content So It's "Extractable"

AI models favor content that's easy to lift verbatim. A study of 3,200 cited passages found that statistic lines get 3.4x more pull than plain narrative, definition sentences get 3.1x, and table rows get 2.7x — so structure your content for extractability.

Specific tactics:
- Include high-quality Q&A sections, use long-tail question-based keywords that mirror natural conversation, publish FAQs that match how customers ask questions, and write clear, structured answers that can be lifted directly.
- Front-load your strongest value propositions — place names, numbers, and key benefits in the first part of sentences and paragraphs.
- For e-commerce/product pages: lead with the use case or "benefit," not the feature — e.g., write "HubSpot helps sales teams of 10–50 people close more deals without manual data entry" instead of "AI-powered pipeline automation."

## 4. Be Specific and Back Up Claims With Evidence

Saying your product is "high-performing" or "the best choice" doesn't give AI much to work with — be specific and provide verifiable information. Similarly, AI models don't recommend vague brands — positioning like "we help businesses grow" gives the AI nothing to work with.

## 5. Build Your Review & Third-Party Presence

This is one of the highest-leverage areas since AI pulls heavily from external sources, not just your own site.

- Optimize your G2 profile — treat it like a landing page with a complete description, feature tags, use case categories, website links, and comparison positioning.
- Claim profiles on **Google Business Profile, G2, Capterra, TrustRadius, Trustpilot, Yelp,** and industry directories, since AI systems love review platforms because they aggregate opinions from many users.
- Ask happy customers for specific, detailed reviews rather than a quick star rating, because the substance of a review gives the model something concrete to repeat.
- Don't overlook community platforms: invest in community platforms, since LLMs pull heavily from Reddit, YouTube, and Wikipedia — Reddit alone has 100 million daily active users generating conversations about brands.

## 6. Create Comparison & Alternative Content

Add comparison content — pages like "Brand X vs. Competitor Y for small business" are exactly what ChatGPT draws from when users are weighing their options.

## 7. Earn Mentions on Trusted Third-Party Sites

Since AI models weight external authority heavily:
- Aim for coverage that describes what you do and who you serve in plain terms, since that is the language ChatGPT reuses when it summarizes you.
- Personalize outreach to journalists/bloggers by referencing specific pieces they've written, and craft a pitch highlighting your unique value, supported by relevant data, testimonials, or case studies.

## 8. Keep Brand Description Consistent Everywhere

Your brand description should be nearly identical across your website, Google Business Profile, LinkedIn, Yelp, Crunchbase, Alignable, industry directories, and anywhere else your brand lives — this consistency acts as a trust signal.

## 9. Track and Iterate

- Use a dedicated AI visibility tracker to see which prompts surface your brand and which name competitors instead, then watch your branded search and direct traffic for the lift those mentions create.
- Tools worth exploring: HubSpot's AEO tracker, Brand24, Mention, or manual prompt testing across ChatGPT/Perplexity/Gemini.

## What NOT to Do
- Don't publish thousands of generic AI-generated pages — more content doesn't automatically create more useful information about your brand.
- Don't chase AI buzzwords — slapping "AI-powered," "AI-ready," or "AI-first" into every headline doesn't make your brand more visible to AI.

---

**Bottom line:** GEO is roughly 80% strategic and 20% technical — focus on positioning, ecosystem presence, and brand authority before worrying about schema and structure. There's no guaranteed formula, but consistent clarity, strong third-party proof, and genuinely useful structured content are the common threads across all current guidance.
